issues.description: Loop invariant is broken: after switching to blocking mode the outer poll-loop's timeout/error handling no longer applies.
issues.detail: The invariant of the outer loop was 'wait with timeout, detect subprocess failure'. Once O_NONBLOCK is cleared and we enter the inner `while True: os.read()`, a writer that opens the FIFO but never closes it (hung child, stuck flush) will block forever with no timeout, no poll, and no exit-detection. State this invariant explicitly or restore the guard.

issues.description: fcntl mode switch is not restored or guarded; exception between F_SETFL and the inner loop leaks blocking state.
issues.detail: The code mutates the fd's flags then enters a read loop with no try/finally. If the caller reuses fifo_fd, or if an exception propagates, the descriptor is left in blocking mode silently. A literate version states the pre/post-condition on fd flags and uses try/finally to make termination of the mode change obvious.

issues.description: The POSIX guarantee cited in the comment is weaker than claimed for FIFOs with multiple potential writers.
issues.detail: Blocking read() on a FIFO returns 0 only when *all* write ends are closed. If any process (including an inherited fd in a grandchild) still holds the write end, the inner loop blocks indefinitely. The comment should state this precondition; otherwise the correctness proof rests on an unverified assumption about who holds the writer fd.

issues.description: Dead `has_blocking_error` bookkeeping and stale comments were removed but the surrounding control flow is now under-commented.
issues.detail: The previous branch carried explanatory prose about macOS EOF quirks and process-exit checks; the replacement collapses to `pass` with a one-liner. A reader auditing this for the same race next year will not see why the non-blocking branch exists at all once data has arrived. Add a literate comment stating: phase 1 = wait-for-first-byte with timeout; phase 2 = drain via blocking read.

issues.description: No test or measurement accompanies a concurrency fix; correctness rests on argument alone.
issues.detail: The PR proves the race away by prose but adds no regression test (e.g., a fixture that writes >64KB then exits immediately) and no measurement that the blocking-drain path is actually exercised. Beware of bugs in the above code; I have only proved it correct, not tried it. A single deterministic test would convert the proof into evidence.

review.summary: The fix correctly identifies a real race between non-blocking reads and kernel pipe buffering, and the two-phase approach (poll-until-first-byte, then drain blocking) is sound in principle. However the patch is UNDER-AUDITED and NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT: the new loop invariant is unstated, the fcntl mode change has no try/finally, and the cited POSIX EOF guarantee silently assumes a single writer fd. The original timeout/process-exit safeguards are removed inside the inner drain loop, so a stuck writer now blocks forever instead of timing out. No test reproduces the original 86KB truncation. Recommend: state the invariant, guard the fd mode change, and add a regression test before merge.
